title: Acme POC Timeline & Milestones
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC to evaluate Redwood inference for Acme's internal assistant. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost, quality), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and a four-milestone timeline: kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review (benchmarks), and exec readout. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send scope & pricing, provide test keys and infra checklist, Acme to provide sample workload, SLA requirements, and a list of stakeholders for the exec readout.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Carter (Acme Head of ML), Lina Gomez (Acme Platform Eng), Tom Park (CTO)

Summary (auto): kickoff and POC milestones for Acme evaluation of Redwood inference. Discussed workload sizing, benchmarks, success metrics (latency/cost/quality), required access and security checks.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - Jordan here, AE. With me is Priya, our SE. Sam, Lina, Tom, thanks for making time. The goal today is to align on a POC timeline and milestones, understand your workload shape, and agree success criteria.

[00:30] Sam (Acme): Yep thanks, Jordan. Quick context - Acme is exploring a POC to migrate a parts of our internal assistant to a hosted/dedicated inference stack. We want to validate latency, cost, and fidelity against our current setup. We have a mix of single-turn prompts and multi-turn chat for diagnostics.

[02:00] Priya (Redwood SE): Great. Can you give an approx workload? QPS, average token lengths, peak patterns? Even ballpark numbers help us size a Dedicated config or recommend hosted call patterns.

[03:05] Sam: We're currently seeing about 8 QPS steady with spikes to 40 during morning hours. Typical prompt length is 80-150 tokens for generation, some embedding calls for retrieval at 512 tokens. Multi-turn sessions average 6 turns. Latency target is p95 under 800ms for generative workflows, ideally p99 under 1.2s - but we want to push for lower. Cost is also a consideration; we want to see cost per 1k tokens and run a few benchmark scenarios.

[05:10] Priya: Helpful. For the POC, we'll recommend two benchmark profiles: 1) interactive gen (low latency, medium tokens) and 2) batch embedding/semantic retrieval (throughput-focused). For the interactive gen, we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token throughput; for embeddings we'll measure throughput (TPS) and 95th percentile latency.

[06:30] Lina (Acme): Security is a big deal for us. We'll need VPC peering or Private deployment options, KMS integration, audit logs retained for 12 months. SOC2 is required. Can Redwood provide a checklist for access and compliance so we can loop in infra and security?

[07:20] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll include a security checklist in the scope doc - VPC peering, IAM roles, KMS, SSL endpoints, SSO/SAML. We have a SOC2 report we can share under NDA. We'll flag what needs to be on the customer side (eg opening certain firewall ports, granting S3 read access to sample datasets).

[09:00] Tom (CTO): Also curious on fallback and graceful degradation. If we route traffic to hosted but need dedicated during spikes, what's the path? Can we do a hybrid routing during the POC?

[09:40] Priya: Yes, hybrid routing is something we can demonstrate. For the POC we'll propose two phases: Phase A (hosted evaluation) to get quick signals and Phase B (dedicated sandbox or private deployment) to validate capacity and isolation. We'll document routing policies and a fallback plan.

[11:15] Sam: Success criteria - let's be explicit: 1) Latency: p95 under 800ms for interactive; p99 under 1.2s. 2) Cost: target a crosswalked cost per 1k generated tokens not exceeding 30% of our current infra spend per unit. 3) Quality: no regression on a hand-labeled prompt set (we'll provide 200 prompts with expected outputs / acceptability flags). 4) Ops: must demonstrate access controls and logging.

[13:00] Priya: Perfect. We'll build a benchmark suite that runs your 200 labeled prompts and measures latency/quality. For quality we'll compute pass/fail on acceptability and surface qualitative diffs.

[15:00] Jordan: Timeline-wise how aggressive do you want to be? Our suggested POC is ~6 weeks with four milestone gates: Kickoff, Access & Setup, Mid-point Review (benchmarks/initial results), and Exec Readout.

[15:40] Sam: 6 weeks sounds reasonable. Can you outline what happens at each milestone?

[16:20] Priya: Sure - Kickoff (this meeting + share docs). Access & Setup (week 1-2): provide API keys or Dedicated sandbox, VPC peering if needed, Redwood runs initial compatibility checks, Acme uploads sample datasets. Mid-point Review (week 3-4): Redwood executes benchmark suite and shares results, we iterate on tuning (batching, quantization recommendations). Final Exec Readout (week 5-6): run final benchmarks, financials, proposed production config, next steps for scale.

[18:30] Lina: For Access & Setup we need a checklist. Also, who owns the infra tasks? Will Redwood be able to run the initial benchmarks from your side or do we need to open access to our test nodes?

[19:15] Jordan: Typically, Redwood can run initial benchmarks using a test harness against the hosted endpoint or dedicated sandbox. For private deployments we need your infra team to complete VPC peering and KMS setup. We'll provide a step-by-step infra checklist and example CloudFormation/Terraform snippets.

[21:00] Sam: Benchmark metrics - besides latency and throughput, we'd like token-level cost breakdown and per-route cost estimates in the results. Is that possible?

[21:45] Priya: Yes - we can produce token-level cost breakdowns and a per-route dashboard. For the POC we'll include a simple cost model comparing current spend vs Redwood predictions. That will be part of the mid-point report.

[23:30] Tom: A quick question on model variants and quantization - if we need lower latency/cost tradeoffs, can Redwood recommend quantized variants and provide guidance on quality impact?

[24:20] Priya: Absolutely. We have quantization profiles and model recommendations based on workload. During tuning we can suggest a quantized 4-bit variant for non-critical flows and run quality regressions against your labeled prompts to measure impact.

[26:00] Sam: For workload sizing, if we hit 40 QPS peaks, what Dedicated config should we expect? Roughly how many GPUs?

[26:40] Priya: Ballpark - depends on model size. For a medium-sized LLM (7B-13B) with our batching and KV caching, 2-4 A100-class GPUs in a dedicated pool could handle those peaks with low latency. We'll produce a sizing recommendation in the scope doc once we have exact prompt length distribution and batchability.

[28:10] Jordan: We'll include a sample cost/throughput table for hosted vs dedicated for your workload shape. Also will include recommended autoscale/burst policies.

[30:00] Sam: Benchmarks - we want reproducible scripts. Can you provide the harness and CI instructions?

[30:25] Priya: Yes - we'll provide a small repo with scripts that run the interactive and embedding tests, collect p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates. We'll also provide guidance on statistical significance and warm-up behaviour (KV cache warm-up etc).

[32:00] Lina: On the security docs - can we get your SOC2 report and details on data residency options? We operate in NA and EU; some data must remain in EU regions.

[32:40] Jordan: We'll share SOC2 report under NDA and outline region options. For the POC we can keep traffic in eu-west-1 regions if you prefer. We'll call out any limits.

[34:00] Sam: Mid-point review - what does a successful mid-point look like?

[34:30] Priya: At mid-point we expect to have run the full benchmark suite, a report showing latency/distribution, cost comparison, and quality regression results on your labeled prompts. If results are promising, we'll iterate on tuning and then finalize for the exec readout. If we fail to meet thresholds, we'll present mitigation options (quantization, different model family, larger dedicated pool) and recommended next steps.

[36:20] Tom: For the exec readout, we'll want a short slide deck with topline numbers, cost delta, recommended prod config, and migration plan. Also bring a list of risks and mitigations.

[37:00] Jordan: Yep - we'll deliver a 10-15 slide exec summary. We'll also include an appendix with raw benchmark logs and scripts.

[38:30] Sam: Any blockers we should flag right now?

[39:00] Lina: Internal infra availability - we'll need to slot time with platform to set up VPC peering. Also legal needs to sign a basic NDA before we exchange SOC2.

[39:25] Jordan: Understood - we'll forward the NDA and the SOC2 access procedure.

[41:00] Priya: Quick note on observability - during the POC we'll enable per-route latency/cost dashboards and provide tracing hooks so your SREs can see token-level traces. That should satisfy the ops folks.

[42:10] Sam: Good. Can we also run a short failover test - simulate a spike and validate fallback to a cheaper model or region?

[42:40] Priya: Yes, we can include a failover scenario in the mid-point benchmark plan. We'll document how to trigger routing policies and measure user impact.

[44:00] Jordan: Recap of milestones and suggested dates: Kickoff (today), Access & Setup (complete by 2025-06-24), Mid-point Review (~2025-07-09), Exec Readout (~2025-07-30). Does that align with Acme's calendar?

[44:30] Sam: Yes those look doable. We'll aim to meet the access & setup date but may need one extra day for platform availability.

[45:15] Tom: For the final readout, can we include cost comparisons for multiple scenarios - hosted, dedicated, private?

[45:35] Jordan: Absolutely - we'll include hosted vs dedicated vs private TCO scenarios.

[46:10] Priya: Anything else on success criteria? We captured latency, cost, quality, and ops. Any additional acceptability thresholds for quality? Sam?

[46:45] Sam: We'll send the pass/fail rubric with the 200 labeled prompts - things like factual accuracy threshold and hallucination tolerance per category.

[48:00] Jordan: Great. We'll draft the scope doc and checklist and send to the group within 48 hours. We'll provision test keys and a small harness by next week. Priya will run the first set of benchmarks once we have the sample prompts.

[50:00] Lina: Legal will want a short addendum about data handling during the POC - we can loop them in after the NDA.

[51:10] Jordan: Noted. Action items and owners will be sent as part of the follow-up email.

[52:00] Sam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the scope doc.

[53:00] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the scope doc, pricing, infra checklist, and schedule invites for the mid-point and final readout. End call.
notes: POC timeline: kickoff (2025-06-18), access/setup by 2025-06-24, mid-point review ~2025-07-09, exec readout ~2025-07-30
Acme to provide 200 labeled prompts + sample datasets; Redwood to provide benchmarks and cost model
